data.name: TipSearchesTheDetailThe
data.value: Searches the detail, the blocked reason and the snooze line together — everything behind the row-s information marker.

data.name: TipShowWhatThisTask
data.value: Show what this task carries, and what is waiting on it

data.name: TipMaterialAndTimeEfficiency
data.value: Material and time efficiency of the blueprint this job would use

data.name: WhatToDoInNote
data.value: What to do, in the order worth doing it. Ranked by how much work each one is holding up, across every tab. The supporting figures are on the tabs themselves.

data.name: TipOpenThisItemIn
data.value: Open this item in the Item Browser

data.name: NothingIsHoldingTheNote
data.value: Nothing is holding the pipeline up: no pool has a queue worth the name, no blueprint has work waiting on it, nothing is short of material, and nothing is waiting on a delivery.

data.name: SlotsAreBandwidthNotNote
data.value: Slots are bandwidth, not a shopping list. A queue is work that piled up while throughput sat under demand, so each remedy is measured by what it does to the time needed to catch up. Rates come from the last 90 days of job history, so they already carry the structures and skills in use.

data.name: MaterialsThePipelineRunsNote
data.value: Materials the pipeline runs out of — the ones nothing owns, not the ones sitting at the wrong station, which is a hauling problem and belongs elsewhere. Ranked by the work each one is holding up. Hover a column heading for what it means. ⚠ Every rate here is a floor: nothing consumed what could not be made, so an item that has been blocking work was used at the rate the blockage allowed rather than the rate that was wanted.

data.name: TipShowTheTasksBehindThese
data.value: Show the tasks behind these counts

data.name: TipTheItemThatRan
data.value: The item that ran short. Click it to open the Item Browser.

data.name: TipConsumedPerDayOver
data.value: Consumed per day over the last 90 days, summed across every blueprint that eats it. An item drawn on by four parents is short four times over.

data.name: TipProducedPerDayOver
data.value: Produced per day over the same window. A dash means nothing here makes it at all, so the only way to refill it is to buy it.

data.name: TipMadePerUnitConsumed
data.value: Made per unit consumed. Under 1.00 the shelf is draining however full it looks, and no size of buffer survives that. Amber rather than red during a demand spike, since absorbing exactly that is what a buffer is for.

data.name: TipWhatTheInventoryLevels
data.value: What the inventory levels ask to keep on the shelf. Blank means no level is set for this at all, which is a finding in its own right.

data.name: TipUnitsTheIndustryScope
data.value: Units the industry scope can actually reach. Stock outside the scope is not counted, because the plan cannot spend it.

data.name: TipWhatTheWorkOn
data.value: What the work on the list wants: what is here plus what it fell short by. Red once that exceeds what exists, which can happen with the level fully met.

data.name: TipTheLevelMeasuredIn
data.value: The level measured in days at the current draw. A buffer is a length of time, not a quantity: 200 of something eaten twice a day is 100 days, and 200 of something eaten 200 times a day is one.

data.name: TipHowMuchHarderThis
data.value: How much harder this is being drawn on now than across the whole window. Blank under 1.2x. This is what separates a build wave from a standing shortage.

data.name: TipTasksThisShortageIs
data.value: Tasks this shortage is holding up: the ones directly short of it, plus the ones stopped for want of what those would have made, and so on up the chain. Tasks, not item types.

data.name: TipJobsMakingThisItem
data.value: Jobs making this item that are installed and running in game right now. Not a task, so nothing on the list asks for it.

data.name: TipTasksToMakeThis
data.value: Tasks to make this item that could be started today.

data.name: TipTasksToMakeThis2
data.value: Tasks to make this item held up only by a busy slot.

data.name: TipTasksToMakeThis3
data.value: Tasks to make this item that are blocked in their own right. Red when nothing is running or ready either, which is the shape that does not resolve on its own.

data.name: TipWhatTheRowAmounts
data.value: What the row amounts to, in a couple of words.

data.name: TipWhatIsHappeningAnd
data.value: What is happening and what would change it, using the figures on this row rather than telling you where to look.

data.name: ABlueprintBottleneckIsNote
data.value: A blueprint bottleneck is having to WAIT for an original to free up — not running one a lot. Ranking on use ranks the fix above the problem: a formula run flat out across eight originals has never blocked anything, and buying the eighth is what settled it. Listed from 5% all-busy up, or 15% for single-BPO items, where the measure degenerates into plain use. Hover a column heading for what it means.

data.name: TipWhatThisBlueprintOr
data.value: What this blueprint or formula makes. Click it to open the Item Browser.

data.name: TipHowLongOneRun
data.value: How long one run takes, averaged over the jobs actually run rather than from the blueprint.

data.name: TipOriginalsOwnedCopiesAre
data.value: Originals OWNED. Copies are deliberately not counted: contention is about whether one of yours was free.

data.name: TipHowManyOfThose
data.value: How many of those originals are sitting inside a job at this moment.

data.name: TipUnitsADayThe
data.value: Units a day the originals on hand could turn out between them, running without a pause.

data.name: TipUnitsADayActually
data.value: Units a day actually produced over the last 90 days. It can never exceed the ceiling, which is why it cannot be used to measure demand.

data.name: TipShareOfEachOriginals
data.value: Share of each original's time spent inside a job. Context only: it does not identify bottlenecks, and ranking on it ranks heavy use above real constraints.

data.name: TipShareOfTheLast
data.value: Share of the last 90 days when EVERY original was occupied at once, counting research and copying as well as building. This is the figure that says whether wanting another job meant waiting.

data.name: TipWhereThisSitsAmong
data.value: Where this sits among all your own blueprints. Nothing here uses a fixed cut-off, so the flag is drawn against your own spread.

data.name: TipTheSameAllBusy
data.value: The same all-busy figure over the last 30 days, so a busy month is not hidden inside a quiet quarter.

data.name: TipWhetherTheRecentSqueeze
data.value: Whether the recent squeeze is rising, easing or steady against the full window.

data.name: TipWhatTheCeilingBecomes
data.value: What the ceiling becomes with one more original. The answer to whether buying one is worth it.

data.name: TipJobsForThisProduct
data.value: Jobs for this product on the worklist right now. Current demand, which history cannot supply.

data.name: TipJobsHeldUpBy
data.value: Jobs held up by the blueprint ALONE. If the product is also short of material, more prints would change nothing, so this counts zero.

data.name: TipTasksWaitingOnWhat
data.value: Tasks waiting on what this makes: directly, and behind those up the chain. A blueprint can be entirely uncontended and still have a queue piled up behind its output.

data.name: TipWhatTheRowAmounts2
data.value: What the row amounts to, in a word.

data.name: TipWhatIsHappeningAnd2
data.value: What is happening and what would change it.

data.name: JobsStoppedForWantNote
data.value: Jobs stopped for want of material that is already owned and sitting somewhere else — the other half of Item Contention, where the fix is a trip rather than a purchase. Every row is a job that could run the moment its material arrives. Hover a column heading for what it means.

data.name: TipTheStoppedJobIt
data.value: The stopped job. It is short of nothing but material already owned, so it runs as soon as that material reaches it.

data.name: TipWhereTheJobWould
data.value: Where the job would run, and so where the material has to arrive.

data.name: TipJobsStoppedBehindThis
data.value: Jobs stopped behind this one: those short of what it would have made, and those behind them up the chain. What starts moving again once this job can run.

data.name: TipDistinctItemTypesThis
data.value: Distinct item types this job is waiting on.

data.name: TipCubicMetresThisJob
data.value: Cubic metres this job is short of, so the trip can be sized before it is planned.

data.name: TipStopsAHaulerWould
data.value: Stops a hauler would have to make to cover what is short, largest source first. NOT the number of hangars holding the item: Tritanium sits in thirteen of them and one covers the job.

data.name: TipHaulsAlreadyOnThe
data.value: Hauls already on the worklist bringing any of this job's missing material to it. Blank is the finding: the material exists, the job is stopped, and nothing is moving it.

data.name: HintFromYyyyMmDd
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: HintThruYyyyMmDd
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: ASourceThatIsNote
data.value: A source that is off is skipped entirely — it costs no queries rather than running and having its output discarded.

data.name: StandingBuyOrdersWhatTo
data.value: Standing buy orders — what to raise

data.name: WhichConditionsBecomeTasksNote
data.value: Which conditions become tasks. Each is a different job, so they switch independently.

data.name: WhereShortfallsAreBoughtNote
data.value: Where shortfalls are bought, and which character maintains orders at each station. Items route through these, so a station with no alt assigned produces blocked items that name no owner.

data.name: HintTradeHub
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: TipWherePurchasesAreRaised
data.value: Where purchases are raised, and whose market alt gets them. Blueprints are left unassigned — a BPO or BPC comes from contracts, not a market order.

data.name: HintStationOrStructure
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: HintCharacter2
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: HintOptional
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: WhenAGroupDropsNote
data.value: When a group drops below the threshold, there should be a buy order at that station. Several rules can point at one group — below 100% order locally, below 75% also order at the hub — and they stack rather than replace each other. Who places the order comes from the station's market alt.

data.name: HintPickAGroup
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: HintTypeTwoCharacters
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: DecidedByTheIndyNote
data.value: Decided by the Indy Park on the Industry tab

data.name: TipBuyPlacesAMarket
data.value: Buy places a market order for the shortfall; Build starts a job for it

data.name: TipRaiseATaskWhen
data.value: Raise a task when stock falls below this share of the group target

data.name: TipFillBackUpTo
data.value: Fill back up to this share of the group target

data.name: TipThisGroupIsSold
data.value: This group is sold or flown, not an input. Work that unblocks it is ranked above work that only refills a buffer.

data.name: WhereEachGroupsStockNote
data.value: Where each group's stock should live. This distributes material rather than demanding more of it — the Inventory Rules already set the quantity — so it raises hauling only, never a buy or a build. Tick Accepts surplus for the station spare stock should collect at when nothing else needs it.

data.name: HintGroup
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: HintNeedNotBeInThe
data.value: Need not be in the park…
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: TipSpareStockOfThis
data.value: Spare stock of this group collects here when no station needs it.

data.name: TipAStationIsLeft
data.value: A station is left alone until it falls this far under its level, then is filled all the way back up. Zero restocks on any shortfall at all.

data.name: SweepSurplusWhenAboveLevel
data.value: Sweep surplus when above level by (%)

data.name: TipExcessIsLeftWhere
data.value: Excess is left where it is until a station is this far over its level, then drained back down to it. Zero sweeps any excess at all.

data.name: WhereIndustryWorkIsNote
data.value: Where industry work is planned, where its materials are counted, and where what is missing gets bought.

data.name: TipDefaultFollowsWhicheverPark
data.value: <Default> follows whichever park is starred in Indy Parks, resolved each time work is planned — so moving the star moves the planning with it.

data.name: TipDaysAShortfallNeeding
data.value: Days. A shortfall needing longer is split into several jobs, which can run on different slots and characters. Blank for no limit — only the blueprint's own run cap then applies.

data.name: TipDaysReactionsAreSet
data.value: Days. Reactions are set apart from manufacturing because they are usually run in shorter, continuous cycles.

data.name: TipDaysCoveringCopyingAnd
data.value: Days, covering copying and invention. This is what decides when one multi-run invention batch becomes two: a batch yields nothing until it ends, and a single attempt on a capital blueprint is already about eight days, so a manufacturing-sized limit would force one attempt per job and spend a science slot on each.

data.name: TipHowFarToLook
data.value: How far to look when deciding a job is short of something. Stock outside this counts as not owned, so it raises a purchase rather than a haul.

data.name: TipOffByDefaultOnly
data.value: Off by default. Only corporations flagged personal on the Corporations tab count as material — authorising a character in a large alliance corp otherwise hands the tool that corp's entire hangar, none of which is yours.

data.name: HintJitaAmarr
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.name: TipTradeHubsYouImport
data.value: Trade hubs you import through. Stock waiting in one of these is stock you have, so it should not raise a second purchase.

data.name: TipClickToRemoveFromThe
data.value: Click to remove from the scope

data.name: StandingProjectsAreDefinedNote
data.value: Standing projects are defined in Corp Activity; the only thing the worklist needs is who maintains them. Projects belong to a corporation, so this routes by corporation rather than by station. Only corporations that actually have standing projects are listed.

data.name: HintPickACorporation
data.comment: Hint in an empty box in WorklistView.

data.comment: Column header: the last 30 days, abbreviated. Keep short.
